Sleep medicine · published research

Sleep bruxism

In a 76-child trial, headache frequency fell after both PBM and splint treatment without a difference between them; bite force was lower after PBM. A 30-child trial reported immediate electromyographic and dopamine changes, but did not establish lasting clinical benefit.

PBM Database summary

What the records report

In a 76-child trial, headache frequency fell after both PBM and splint treatment without a difference between them; bite force was lower after PBM. A 30-child trial reported immediate electromyographic and dopamine changes, but did not establish lasting clinical benefit.

Summary of the Evidence

The exact Sleep medicine > Bruxism category contains five titles: two pediatric randomized trials and three protocols. Two adjacent records also map to this indication: a protocol under Oral > Bruxism and a systematic review under Oral > TMD. The review synthesizes the same completed pediatric trials, and none of these records adds a new patient cohort.

Human and clinical evidence

Salgueiro et al. randomized 76 children to PBM at acupuncture points, occlusal splint, sham light, or control. Headache frequency improved in both the PBM and splint groups, with no significant difference between those treatments. Bite force was lower in the PBM group, while salivary cortisol rose across groups (2021). A second randomized trial included 30 children, ten per group, and reported immediate electromyographic and salivary-dopamine differences after infrared LED treatment; the small sample and short assessment do not show durable bruxism control (Kobayashi et al. 2022). A mapped systematic review of pediatric bruxism synthesized these same PBM and splint studies rather than adding a new cohort (Al Fallaha et al. 2026). Protocol publications describe these lines of investigation rather than independent outcomes (Salgueiro et al. 2020).

Animal evidence

No animal experiment is listed for sleep bruxism.

In-vitro and ex-vivo evidence

No standalone cell or ex-vivo study is listed.

Treatment Parameters and Generalizability

The 76-child trial used 786.94-nm laser at 33.5 J/cm2 for 20 seconds per point across 12 acupoints. The other trial used infrared LED. Wavelength names the light's color band and affects tissue penetration. Pediatric point-based protocols cannot be assumed to work for adults or for objectively measured sleep bruxism.

Interpretation

The trials report selected short-term changes but do not show that PBM is superior to splint care or that it prevents ongoing nocturnal episodes. Future trials should use polysomnography or validated objective measures, adequate sham control, and follow-up beyond treatment.

Evidence strength in source summaryLow for short-term headache, bite-force, or electromyographic outcomes in two small pediatric trials Very low for sustained control of sleep bruxism or superiority to established care
Publications and records7 relevant titles (5 exact Sleep medicine > Bruxism plus 1 mapped Oral > Bruxism protocol and 1 mapped Oral > TMD systematic review)

Evidence strength rationale and next steps

Two pediatric randomized trials report selected short-term changes, but one found similar headache improvement with PBM and a splint, and the other had only 30 participants with immediate outcomes. Protocol papers repeat planned studies rather than add cohorts. Larger blinded trials need objective sleep measures and longer follow-up.
